conviction_note: The release is confirmed for the morning of 13 Nov. I found no company-level number the market has not seen. The small positive lean comes from two things: CoreWeave's 10 Nov beat-and-raise, which MRL barely tracked (+0.6% against CRWV +24.7%), and a FY26 FFO guide of EUR340m that, after EUR180m in H1, implies a flat H2. Against that, this name sold its July guidance raise (-2.9% that day, -2.4% the next) and fell 5.2% on last year's 9M. So p_up 54 on an abs_move of 4.0, scaled +0.32. The findings sum to +1.4 and are each sized on their own; the gap is the reaction-history veto, which acts on p_up only.

already_public.what: H1 2026 results: FFO EUR180.0m (+8.0%), GRI EUR291.7m, LTV 24.5%, NTA EUR15.99. FY26 FFO guide raised to EUR340m (EUR0.55 p.s.). 160 MW let or pre-let, 'on track to far exceed' the 200 MW IT leasing guide, 180 MW in Lisbon 'in advanced negotiations'.
Nebius leases 18 MW at Madrid-Getafe, diversifying away from CoreWeave
Merlin says CoreWeave is 8.6% of total rents (about 80% of the data-centre business) and rules out impacts
Bankinter cuts to Neutral with a EUR13.6 target (from 19.6), citing the data-centre Real Decreto, CoreWeave credit and rising yields; confirms 9M results Friday 13 Nov before the open
EUR3.75bn sustainable corporate syndicated financing signed to restructure debt and fund the data-centre programme (MRL +1.8% that day)

new_in_release.expect: FY26 FFO EUR340m reiterated, with a modest raise possible. The guide implies H2 of about EUR160m against H1's EUR180m, partly explained by the November 2026 refinancing cost. Lean slightly up.
9M FFO around EUR255-265m (9M25 was about EUR245m). Expected in line to slightly above the run-rate the guide implies.

Data-centre leasing update: MW let against the 200 MW guide, whether a Lisbon contract has been signed, whether Phase III is being paced, and commentary on CoreWeave and the Real Decreto. Direction unknown; this is the line the stock trades on.
An interim dividend, about EUR0.20 last year (paid December 2025). Expected flat to slightly up.
Debt cost after the EUR3.75bn refinancing, and LTV. Unknown.

findings.finding: CoreWeave (about 80% of Merlin's data-centre MW and 8.6% of its rents) reported Q3 2026 on 10 Nov: revenue $3.66bn, backlog $132.5bn and FY26 revenue guidance raised to $13.0-13.3bn. CRWV closed +24.7% on 11 Nov, yet MRL rose only +0.6% that day and was down about 0.8% intraday on 12 Nov. One of Bankinter's two 'tormenta perfecta' pillars (tenant credit) eased, and the 9M call is the first chance for management to restate tenant exposure after it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Tenant-credit worry was cited when MRL fell in Oct 2026 (Bankinter downgrade 22 Oct). After Merlin said CoreWeave was 8.6% of rents (19 Oct), the stock was flat to down. There is no clean prior on a relief print.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market had priced the tenant relief, MRL would have re-rated alongside CRWV on 11 Nov. It moved +0.6% against +24.7% and gave that back on 12 Nov. This is still a counterparty proxy, not a Merlin number, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: The Bankinter note naming CoreWeave's credit as a driver of the de-rating: https://www.merca2.es/2026/10/22/bankinter-merlin-tormenta-2478217/ ; CRWV closes 48.73 to 60.77 from https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/CRWV?range=10d&interval=1d

findings.finding: The FY26 FFO guide of EUR340m after H1 FFO of EUR180m implies H2 of only about EUR160m. That is below the H1 run-rate and roughly flat on H2 2025 (FY25 EUR327m minus H1 2025 about EUR167m). The guide therefore leaves room for a reiteration with upside, or another raise, at 9M, offset partly by November refinancing costs.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The H1 2026 guide raise (to EUR340m) was sold: -2.94% on 28 Jul and -2.36% on 29 Jul. The 9M25 print fell 5.17% on 14 Nov 2025. The FY25 print (27 Feb 2026) rose 5.04%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is arithmetic on public numbers, so partly priced. Sell-side focus since August has been data-centre regulation and tenant risk, not core FFO run-rate. If the market expected a raise, the stock would not be 16% down over 60 days with consensus targets being cut. It is an inference, not a disclosed number, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: The Spanish press reported the H1 guide as 'aumentar en un 4% su previsión de beneficio recurrente ... hasta los 340 millones' (https://www.elespanol.com/invertia/empresas/inmobiliario/20260728/merlin-gana-millones-junio-eleva-previsiones/1003744335988_0.amp.html). That is the same fact, not independent.

findings.finding: At H1 Merlin said it was 'on track to far exceed the FY26 200 MW IT leasing guidance', with 180 MW in Lisbon 'in advanced negotiations'. The 9M update is the first checkpoint on whether more leases have been signed since the 18 MW Nebius lease (2 Sep).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Data-centre leasing news drove the FY25 print (+5.0%). At H1 2026, leasing ahead of plan did not stop a -2.9% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Exceeding 200 MW lands inside what the company already guided, so most of it is expected. Only a signed Lisbon contract or a Phase III pause would be new, and I found no source for either.

findings.finding: On 2 Nov Merlin signed EUR3.75bn of sustainable corporate syndicated financing to restructure corporate debt and fund the data-centre programme. It addresses the funding doubt behind Bankinter's 'standby' scenario, and the 9M release will show its cost and its effect on LTV.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: MRL rose +1.8% on the announcement day (2 Nov 2026). The March 2026 EUR768m placement funded Phase III.
findings.original_quote: Merlin Properties ha anunciado este lunes que ha suscrito una financiación sostenible corporativa por un importe de 3.750 millones de euros (Merlin Properties announced this Monday that it has signed sustainable corporate financing of EUR3.75bn)
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the stock rose 1.8% that day. Only the cost of the new debt, still unseen, is left. What the money buys is the data-centre build-out with leases already signed (160 MW let), so it is signed positive.
findings.independence: Bankinter's 'standby' scenario rests on funding doubts: https://www.merca2.es/2026/10/22/bankinter-merlin-tormenta-2478217/

outside_window.finding: The data-centre Real Decreto (new renewables covering 80% of consumption, verified hourly, for sites of 1 MW or more) has about 600 submissions after public consultation and no date for the Consejo de Ministros. If approved as drafted it would put Merlin's Phase III in question. Its resolution date is unknown and probably after 13 Nov. Management commentary on the call is a two-sided in-window risk, but no sourced fact says which way it goes.

baseline_tension: The small positive lean agrees in sign with the +3.95% 20-day / +4.88% 5-day run-up, which is the free control and the whole of the lean. It is not orthogonal to the control, which is one more reason p_up stays near 50.
language_note: The session came from Spanish sources: merca2 says 'antes de apertura del mercado' and the Europa Press/Bolsamanía timestamp puts last year's 9M at 08:22 CET. The English aggregators gave conflicting dates (12 or 13 Nov).

Bankinter's downgrade thesis (Real Decreto, CoreWeave credit, target 19.6 to 13.6) and the EUR3.75bn financing came from Spanish press (merca2, Alicante Plaza/EFE). The English searches did not surface them.
The draft decree's terms (80% hourly new-renewables coverage, about 600 submissions, no Consejo de Ministros date) came from Spanish sources.
lessons_applied: 'The move is in the guide': a 9M FFO guide change is plausible given the conservative implied H2, so abs_move_pct went from 3.5 to 4.0 (this name's results-day moves are 2.2-5.2%).
'Lands inside what the company guided': the leasing finding ('far exceed 200 MW' is already guided) went from +0.3 to +0.2.
'Proxy / counterparty transmission': the CoreWeave finding went from +0.6 to +0.5.
'Financing is a question': the loan is already priced (+1.8% on 2 Nov), so that finding went from +0.2 to +0.1. Its sign stays positive because the money funds leased capacity.
'This name sells its beats' (the H1 raise was sold for -2.9%): p_up went from 55 to 54.
